census.method:
Script versions are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-v2d-track3/8c892c5e-fd7c-57aa-abef-68d2af098e4f/scratchpad/interact/ (census1.py, vox2.py). Inputs: our tracks loc/perc/ep<N>/poses.npz (world_T_cam, cam_T_<obj>), object names and slot order from result.json, and our meshes: library_v2 for everything, plus v4 for the boards and v3 for the sweeper.

(1) Solid samples. For each mesh, the centres of a 2 mm grid in its body frame that warp's BVH winding-number query (CPU) classes as inside. This gives an unbiased volume: sample volume matches mesh volume within 1% (pot 621.6 vs 624.6 cm3; wp2 is the exception, 281 vs 323, because trimesh's volume is unreliable on it).

(2) Overlap, every frame, both orders. T_BA = inv(cam_T_B[t]) @ cam_T_A[t]. A's samples are mapped into B; those inside B's bounding box (+1 mm) get B's exact signed distance (winding sign). Overlap = count x 8 mm3. Penetration = the largest inside distance. A-in-B and B-in-A agree within about 0.1 cm3 (ep24 at the peak: 10.95 vs 11.01). Reported overlap = mean of the two directions.

(3) Contact = minimum distance between 40k surface samples of each mesh (cKDTree) below 5 mm.

(4) Region bookkeeping. Overlap frames = mean overlap above 1 cm3. Each sample keeps a count of the overlap frames in which it lies inside the partner, in its own object frame. From that: union; core50 / core80 (samples inside in at least 50% / 80% of overlap frames); persistence (share of each frame's overlap that lies in core50); mean pairwise Jaccard; centroid standard deviation; core bounding box. An object is 'moving' when its world displacement exceeds 4 mm per frame (5-frame median). Relative-pose jitter = |relative translation minus its 9-frame median|.

(5) Diagnostics, public episodes only, never method inputs:
- (a) The same census with the mocap relative pose (the parquet 'pose' field is in the scan frame, which is our mesh frame). This gives the overlap caused by the meshes alone.
- (b) Public scans posed by mocap, as the floor of the method. Only for scans that are reliable solids (winding and pseudo-normal volumes agree within 5%: boards, sweeper, dust pan, pitcher); the cup, pot, lid and rack scans read their cavities as solid.
- (c) Scans posed by our tracks, for ep18, ep23 and ep24.
- (d) Each core50 sample's distance and pseudo-normal side relative to its own object's scan surface.

(6) Table check. recon_mesh.table_plane RANSAC on our frame-0 depth, plus an independent fit on the last frame's depth moved to world by our camera odometry. Only ep2, ep18 and ep27 have depth caches locally. For ep23 and ep24, a support plane through the boards' lowest points at frame 0 (the boards lie flat; their thin axes are parallel within 1.1-1.4 deg). Reference parquets: table top at z = 0.60.

An earlier version (census.py, 2.5 mm nearest-voxel lookup, kept in census/grid_v0) was replaced: voxel rounding at contact faces shifts each surface by up to 1.25 mm, which across tens of cm2 of contact is several cm3.

Cost: all 13 episodes took about 10 min wall on 3 processes (CPU shared with other jobs); the mocap diagnostic about 10 min; the table check 5 min.

Caveat: these loc/perc tracks were made with the public scans as the FoundationPose template (reg.log says "meshes": "public scans"). The census logic only needs inference-legal inputs, but in production it must run on tracks made with our own meshes (perc2m).

census.table_support:
Our own depth plane, frame 0 (RANSAC with recon_mesh.table_plane; inlier fraction 0.12-0.21). Lowest-point height in cm; negative means below the plane. Mesh value first, scan value (diagnostic, scan posed by our tracks) second:
- ep2: pot -0.67 / -0.54 cm. Lid 7.98 / 8.67 cm (it rests on the pot).
- ep18: sweeper -0.96 (v2) / -0.69 (v3) / -0.76 (scan) cm. Dust pan -0.64 / -0.18 cm.
- ep27: rack -1.25 / -1.24 cm. Pot -0.52 / -0.56 cm.

So at frame 0 our tracks put objects 0.2-1.3 cm into our table, with the scan as well as with our mesh. That is a track or plane bias, not floating; the mesh adds at most 0.1-0.5 cm (dust pan 0.46 cm). Medians over the first rest segment are within 0.3 cm of frame 0. An independent plane from the last frame's depth is tilted 0.6-1.6 deg from the frame-0 plane and offset 0.2-2 mm. Last rest of the ep27 pot: +1.1 / +2.0 cm, because it sits on the rack.

Floating from our tracks, ep23/ep24. Support plane taken from the boards lying flat at frame 0. With the X assembled and standing (thin axes within 1 deg of horizontal), the boards' lowest points are 3.2-4.0 cm above that plane in ep24 and 1.2-2.0 cm in ep23. With mocap poses (diagnostic) our v4 boards are only 0.74-0.77 cm up and the scans 0.31-0.43 cm. So at most about 0.5 cm of the float comes from our mesh shape and 2.5-3.5 cm from our tracks and odometry. Also under mocap at frame 0, our boards' lowest points are 0.4-0.8 cm below the scans' (bottom face too low or too thick) and our dust pan's is 0.5 cm below.

References (mkref snaps everything to the table at frame 0, so h = 0 there). Last frame: ep24 wp1 3.99 cm and wp2 2.69 cm above the table; ep27 pot 2.58 cm (it rests on the rack); ep12 cup 0.78 cm (in the rack); ep18 0.26 / 0.26 cm; racks -0.03 / -0.14 cm.
conclusions: Overlap is mostly a mesh property, not track noise. Placed with mocap relative poses, our meshes overlap about as much as with our tracks: ep24 10.5 vs 10.4, ep23 10.2 vs 10.5, ep2 20.5 vs 23.2, ep12 3.4 vs 3.2, ep13 2.5 vs 1.5, ep11 42.7 vs 52.7, ep31 5.7 vs 4.1 cm3 (medians over the same frames). Scans placed with mocap overlap at most 0.88 cm3 (ep24), 1.2 (ep23) and 1.6 (ep18): that is the floor of the method. Penetration depths are 6-12 mm while the relative jitter of our tracks is 0.7-2 mm (median). The exception is ep0, where the lid track is flipped (179 deg, 44 mm): 86.5 cm3 with our tracks against 23.5 with mocap.

The boards (ep23, ep24) give the cleanest, reproducible signal. Fully inserted, the overlap is a 1.0 x 11.2-11.4 x 1.2 cm column across wp1's width at mid-length, 10.8-10.9 cm3, CV 0.02-0.03, centroid std 1.3-1.5 mm. The centroid is the same in both episodes within 1 mm: (0.0, -0.5, 0.4) vs (0.0, -0.4, 0.4) cm. During insertion it grows down from wp1's +y edge (1.4-2.4, then 5.0-5.2, then 10.8 cm3). In each board's frame, the +y half of the column lies outside the real board (7-29% inside the scan) and the -y half inside (66-70%). So the column is exactly the two missing notches, split near y = 0. The real notches are about 0.8 cm wide (board thickness 8 mm). Our wp2 is 12 mm thick, which widens the column. Flattening the edges (v4) does not change the joint (+0.15 cm3).

The insertion motion says which object gets which part of the column. wp2 travelled along wp1's -y from y = +17 cm to 0, with its own y axis antiparallel. For a cross-halving joint, each board's notch must open at the edge the partner entered from (wp1 +y, wp2 +y), and both scans confirm it. The motion does not fix where the column is split; a half-width prior matches the scans. Hypothesis H-I1: carving each board by the partner's swept solid, limited to the board's own entry half, removes at least 80% of the 10.8 cm3 and recovers a notch of about 0.8-1.2 cm. To falsify: rebuild, then measure overlap at the assembled pose under mocap (target at most 1.2 cm3, the scan floor), plus the boards' standing stability and registered AUC on ep23/24.

Lid on pot (ep2; ep0 under mocap) is the second strong, reproducible case. A ring 20-25 cm3 deep 7.5-8 mm sits in the pot's rim band (pot x about +6 cm) and in the lowest 1.4-1.8 cm of the lid. With mocap poses our lid's lowest point is 7.7 mm below the scanned lid's (8.07 vs 8.84 cm above the table), and our pot rim is only 1 mm high. So the excess is in the lid's lower ring (a filled underside). Constraint: the lid must rest on the rim, so shave or lift about 8 mm of the lid's lower ring. The dome cavity above the pot's empty interior is not constrained by this contact.

Cups. In ep11 the cups are nested (mocap: the blue cup sits 3.1-3.2 cm above the beige cup on a shared axis) and our meshes overlap 42.7 cm3 over the whole wall height (8.8 x 8.6 x 13 cm, 9 mm deep), so walls are too thick or the cavity too narrow. Our tracks also sink the inner cup about 2.7 cm. Cup in rack (ep12, ep13): small but very stable (1.5-3.4 cm3, 6-8 mm, centroid std 0.16 cm in ep12). The excess is on the cup's end in ep12 (57% of the core more than 3 mm outside the cup scan, against 7% for the whole cup) but in the rack's slot in ep13 (100% more than 3 mm from the rack scan, median 9.8 mm, against 25%). Overlap alone cannot say which object to carve; a tie-breaker is needed, for example whether the region was observed as surface in the TSDF or only filled from unknown (this needs the TSDF state, which the library does not keep).

Contacts to exclude. Sweeper brushing the rack (ep31): the overlap is fixed in the sweeper frame (bristle edge, core50 2.6 cm3) but slides in the rack frame (core50 0, centroid std 9.4 cm, relative spread 94 mm and 38 deg). Sweeper into pan (ep18): transient (1 frame with our tracks, 8 with mocap, max 9.3 cm3), and even the rigid scans overlap up to 1.6 cm3 under mocap, consistent with bristles bending. Proposed rule: carve only regions that are persistent (at least 50% of overlap frames), fixed in BOTH object frames (centroid std at most about 0.5 cm), seen while the relative pose is static or sliding along one axis (insertion), and deeper than 3 times the track jitter (3 mm or more). Exclude bristles and other compliant parts.

No usable constraint: ep21/22 pouring never touches (minimum distance 74.6 / 47.5 mm); ep27 pot on rack is clean (at most 0.35 cm3, 3.2 mm), so our pot and rack are compatible there; ep26's rack track is broken (455 cm path, 13 cm jumps) and the episode was excluded. Usable constraint sources among the 13 episodes: ep23, ep24 (slots), ep2 (and ep0 once its lid track is fixed: lid ring), ep11 (nesting), ep12, ep13 (rack slot or cup end).

Table. At frame 0 objects sit 0.2-1.3 cm BELOW our depth table plane, with the scans as well as with our meshes. The 1-4 cm float in the references builds up later from our tracks: the assembled X in ep24 is 3.2-4.0 cm above the frame-0 board plane (ep23 1.2-2.0 cm), while under mocap our boards rise only 0.74-0.77 cm (scans 0.31-0.43). So table contact is a weak shape constraint here (our boards' bottom faces are 0.4-0.8 cm low, the dust pan 0.5 cm). It is better used to re-anchor rest poses at the end of an episode, which is a fix to tracking and odometry drift, not to the mesh.

Rule caveat: these loc/perc tracks were made with the public scans as the FoundationPose template (reg.log: "meshes": "public scans"). The census uses only inference-legal quantities (tracks, our meshes, names), but for submissions it must be run on tracks made with our own meshes. All mocap and scan numbers above are diagnostics on public episodes only.

The repo was not modified (the repo pipeline was imported with bytecode writing disabled). Earlier grid-lookup results are kept in census/grid_v0; they overstate small contacts by voxel rounding and are superseded by census1.

defects.method:
This was a diagnostic run only. It reads public scans and mocap and is not part of any method. Inputs were meshes/library_v2 (10 objects that have a public scan; wooden_spoon has none) and loc/perc tracks. No repo file was changed.

(1) Registration. Two-sided trimmed ICP (70% inliers) from the identity, run on 20k/80k surface samples. Our track body frame already matches the scan frame: corrections were 0.16–3.3 deg and 0.7–3.6 mm. Residuals ours->scan were median 0.8–5.2 mm and p90 3.2–17 mm. Fitted scale was 0.995–1.007, so there is no size bias.

(2) Solids on a 2 mm grid in the scan frame. Our meshes are watertight after vertex merge, so ray parity was used for them. Scans are not watertight, so the generalized winding number (warp, thresholds 0.3/0.5/0.7) was used. Three scans miss inner surfaces: beige_cup, blue_cup and white_pot. For these the winding volume depends on the threshold (pot: 2220/1112/379 cm3). They were repaired by visibility: a voxel is free if one of 1024 rays escapes. Wall voxels within the measured wall thickness (2.2/2.6/3.5 mm) of the surface were kept. Result: 121/136/357 cm3 instead of 447/547/1112.

(3) Excess = ours solid & scan empty. Missing = the reverse. Both are split by distance band. Excess is located by concavity width: closing(scan, r) − scan for r = 6/10/20/45 mm, the rest of the convex hull, and outside the hull by side.

(4) Thickness: 30k scan-surface samples. Scan thickness is the ray along −normal. Ours is the inside interval of our mesh on the same line.

(5) Stable poses: convex-hull support regions (normals within 3 deg, contact within 1.5 mm), uniform-density centre of mass (COM) of the voxel solid, and tip angle = atan(margin / COM height). For each scan pose with tip >= 2 deg, I took the best of ours within 10 deg.

(6) Interactions, all 20 public episodes, stride 2. The other object was placed in this object's frame three ways:
- its scan with our tracks;
- OUR mesh with our tracks (the realistic input a method can use);
- its scan with mocap (upper bound).
MediaPipe hand capsules (r 7 mm) were placed with our tracks. The union over frames (thresholds >=1/3/10/30 frames) was intersected with our excess ("carve") and with real scan material ("conflict" = what a carve would wrongly remove). Per-frame overlap volumes and 4 mm contact shells against missing volume were also computed.

CPU only; each step took under 8 min.

Mechanism, in order of weight:
1. Too few unoccluded views of the empty slot leave many slot voxels unknown (fewer than 3 observations).
2. The fill rule (lines 249-252) marks every unknown component that does not touch the grid border as inside, and an unknown slot is enclosed by walls and by carved space above it. This alone takes the 9 mm slot from 96 % to 26 % free under ideal depth. It also thickens the board by 6 mm.
3. Truncation of 12 mm is larger than the slot width and about equal to the board thickness. Rays hitting the faces and slot walls in front of a slot voxel leave it within 12 mm behind a surface, so it gets negative votes: 30 % of slot voxels end inside, mean −0.19. With 4 mm truncation that becomes 0 % inside.
4. The 4 mm voxel puts the slot at 1-2 voxels. The Gaussian (sigma 0.8 voxel, lines 278-279) closes a 1-voxel gap (centre value −0.01) and keeps a 2-voxel gap (+0.43).
5. In the real data, half-resolution stereo across a 3-6 px gap plus the 2 cm 5x5 edge filter (lines 128-131) remove most of the depth that remains. This step is a hypothesis: the ep23 depth cache is not local.

Not causes: merge_vox (dilation is used only for labelling, line 268-277), the parts filter (288-292) and decimation (see the downstream risks). Separate bug: table_plane line 89 calls np.linalg.svd without full_matrices=False and allocates an N x N matrix. On real data that is about 2 GB transient; on a clean synthetic table it needed 45.6 GB and crashed. I worked around it in my own process only.
integration_points: Shared, multi-object fusion driver: recon_mesh.py:227-240 (main) builds one grid per object and calls integrate per episode. Mutual exclusion needs one driver that holds the grids of every object in an episode (each in its own object frame) and visits frames jointly. Also save vol/wgt after line 241 (np.savez) so a later stage can redo closing with constraints without re-fusing.

Per-frame volumetric exclusion and swept volume: integrate() between line 183 (other-object masking) and 184 (keep rule), in the same style as below_carve (158-164). Transform this object's voxel centres X into the other object's frame with inv(T_oo[t]) @ T_co[t]. Voxels inside the other object's current solid (its SDF/occupancy grid, not a KD-tree of surface points as now at lines 103-106) get a free vote with weight w_excl. Applied over the insertion frames (ep23 f150-252, ep24 f135-213) this is the swept-volume constraint. At co-located frames (centre distance < 1 cm) it is the assembly constraint. Who gives up the overlap must be decided by evidence: the voxel goes to the object with more confident observed-inside votes from its own depth, alternating or jointly. Margin = tracking error.

Other-object masking itself: lines 99-106 and 177-183 use the posed PUBLIC SCAN as the other mesh in every library build. It must become our own current reconstruction (iterated), both for compliance and so the exclusion is consistent.

Constraint-aware closing: recon_mesh.py:249-265. AND solid_fill (252) and solid_near (253) with NOT interaction_free, so fill can never turn voxels claimed free by exclusion, swept volume or hand volume back into solid. Closing alone took the ideal 9 mm slot from 96 % to 26 % free.

Thin-feature resolution: --voxel / --trunc defaults at lines 197-198 and the Gaussian at 278-279 (sigma 0.8 voxel closes 1-voxel gaps). The 2 mm / 4 mm variant (--half 0.15) kept the slot (94.5 % free). It needs 'near' closing, because with 4 mm truncation 65 % of a 9 mm board's interior is unknown. Options: a second, finer grid only around predicted contact or insertion regions, or adaptive truncation.

Table band versus thin objects: lines 156-157 and 216-217 (table_band 0.015). A 9 mm board lying flat never votes for a surface. Make the band adaptive (for example 3-5 mm with the per-frame refit) or object-aware.

Support contact as a shape constraint: lines 158-164 (below_carve) are the free-space half. The contact half (a flat patch where the perceived resting object touches the plane, which flatten_base.py:16-22 does by hand) should be added inside fusion or in the constraint stage. It would trigger automatically from rest segments detected in our tracks (contact_retarget.py:304 rest_settle has the static or no-hand detection). Stability check: contact_retarget.py:277 stable_ups, run on the CoACD pieces.

Hand volume as free space and fingertip contacts: lines 37-55 (hand_segments) and 165-176. The capsules currently only drop samples. Add free votes for voxels inside finger-core capsules (about 7-8 mm) and surface votes or inside-boundary priors at fingertips that mkref/contact_retarget classify as in contact (mkref.py:527 depenetrate already computes object SDF queries).

Simulator collision geometry: make_assets.py:28-35 writes one <collision> mesh equal to the visual mesh, and lines 55-62 strip colours. FlashCHORD then runs CoACD on it (flash_chord/scene/objects.py:159-210 → assets/mesh.py:62-96, threshold 0.05, max_convex_hull -1, preprocess_mode 'auto', other CoACD defaults; configs/scene/{train,eval}.yaml decompose_objects: true; scene/setup.py:68-85 never passes decompose_params, which builder.py:431 would accept). To keep a slot, write our own convex pieces as several <collision> elements: decompose ourselves with a slot-respecting split or a lower threshold, then verify. Each convex piece then returns one hull. Patching the threshold through ops/box/patch_flashchord.py changes the evaluator, which is a compliance risk.

Validation gate after assets: scratchpad overlap_vol.py (overlap of HullSDF pieces at reference frames) and tools/frame_quality_probe.py (assist-off drop/pop test). Both belong after make_assets as automatic checks: overlap at co-located frames below about 1 cm³; stable at rest segments.
downstream_risks: Decimation (kit v2dlb/mesh_budget.py:8-35, fast_simplification QEM to ≤ 4096 faces and vertices, then padding with degenerate faces) is NOT a risk. Measured (slot_mk.py): synthetic boards with 4 / 6 / 9 / 17 mm through-slots kept 100 % of the slot free after budget_mesh (116k → 4096 faces), and rays through the scans' 4-6 mm slots still pass after budgeting. Note: the library .glb files are the coloured full-resolution meshes, not budgeted (board 1 8,208 faces). recon_mesh's own budget output (lines 294-299) is unused. Budgeting happens only at packing (track3_pose.py:202-222 pack_object_meshes) and in score_registered/recon_eval.

CoACD in the simulator IS a blocker for a ~9 mm slot. Measured (slot_coacd.py, coacd 1.0.11 with FlashCHORD's parameters): a clean board with a 4 / 6 / 9 mm slot → 1 hull, slot volume 99-100 % covered (fully refilled). 17 mm slot → 3 hulls, 0 % covered. The budgeted public scans (other concavities: legs, arch, pegs) → 7 / 12 hulls: the slot centre line stays free but 27-37 % of the slot volume is covered, so the effective slot is narrower than the mating board. Conclusion: even a perfect slotted mesh will collide as overlapping boards unless we supply our own convex pieces (make_assets.py:28-35). Caveat: whether the organisers would rebuild assets from the submitted 4096-face mesh with default CoACD if they re-ran policies is unknown.

Scorer registration (track3_pose.py:54-65): 3,000 surface samples per mesh, centroid plus scale normalised to the scan's surface radius, then _align_rigid. The slot walls are about 2 % of a board's surface area, so having or lacking a slot barely moves registration or CD-O. Wrong thickness matters far more: fill closing thickened the synthetic 9 mm board to 1.4 cm, our library boards measure 0.78 / 1.2 cm median against 0.8-0.9 cm in the scan, and the sensitivity test gave 0.608 AUC for 5 mm inflation plus board flips. A slot-aware method should not hurt scoring, provided carving does not thin or shift the boards asymmetrically. Run recon_eval flip rate / registered AUC on ep23/24 after any change.
make_assets (lines 55-62) re-welds with process=True and drops colours. It keeps the geometry, so a slot would survive. Newton splits by colour only when colours are present.

Real-depth risk not measured here: FoundationStereo at half resolution (depths_fs0.5, 1000x1600 cache) puts 3-6 px across the slot, and the 2 cm edge filter removes about 2 px on each side. Even with fusion fixed, the empty slot may simply not be in the depth. Hypothesis; test by downloading the ep23/ep24 depth caches and inspecting slot pixels in the frames where it is open. That is why evidence from interactions (exclusion and swept volume from our tracks) is needed, not only better carving.

Tracking error at the assembled pose: the scans themselves overlap about 4 cm³ at our tracks (reviewer's figure, not rechecked). Exclusion carving therefore needs a margin or a robust weight, or it will carve too much (holes through thin walls) or push the error into the shape.

sources.title: Where Does It End? Reasoning About Hidden Surfaces by Object Intersection Constraints (Co-Section), Strecke & Stückler
sources.verified: Opened the arXiv abstract and the full text on ar5iv. It is a backend on EM-Fusion's per-object TSDFs. It adds a hull constraint, E_hull = β∫ max{0, d_hull − u}^2 over observed free space (the 'unseen' hull is everything hidden behind seen surfaces or outside the view), and a time-indexed intersection constraint d_inter^o(x) = max_t max_p (−u^p(T_p,t^-1 T_o,t x)): the deepest any point of object o ever goes inside another object p over all time steps. E_inter penalises u^o < d_inter. They avoid the chicken-and-egg problem by using point measurements (a weighted mean of observed SDF samples) for the other object's SDF. Results on Co-Fusion car4 (accuracy / completeness, lower is better, presumably metres): TSDF truck 0.0095 / 0.0376 → Co-Section 0.0088 / 0.0110; car 0.0020 / 0.0277 → 0.0052 / 0.0102; third object 0.0365 / 0.0281 → 0.0872 / 0.0162. Completeness improves 1.7–3.4x, but accuracy gets worse on 2 of the 3 objects. Intersection term under 10 ms per volume on GPU; optimisation averages 0.98 s (peak 19.8 s) at 64^3 per object. The ablation says intersection without hull creates spurious zero crossings; hull plus intersection is needed.
sources.method: Variational SDF completion (Hessian-IMLS data term) with two constraints: observed free space caps the surface, and the max-over-time penetration into other tracked objects is pushed out.
sources.code: github.com/EmbodiedVision/cosection (C++/CMake on EM-Fusion with Mask R-CNN). GPL-3.0 per the README; commercial use needs a separate licence.
sources.use_for_us: This is the closest published match to the owner's idea. Our recon_mesh already fuses a TSDF per object in the object frame and already has every object's per-frame cam_T. The d_inter term carries over directly: map each voxel of A into B's frame for every frame and take the maximum depth inside B's confident core; carve A where that exceeds a margin. The hull constraint corresponds to giving observed free space priority over closure fill. Measured on our ep24 tracks with our library_v2 meshes (scratch script interact/tools/ep24_rel.py, 2 mm voxels): end-state overlap is 16.2–16.4 cm^3 from t≈220 to 275; time-max penetration >4 mm covers 11.8 cm^3, a 1.2 x 11.4 x 1.2 cm column in board-1's frame.
sources.effort: About 1 day CPU. It is a post-pass on saved per-object TSDF/weight grids, so recon_mesh must save them. It can be prototyped locally on ep2 (pot + lid), ep18 and ep27, whose depth caches are local; ep24 needs its depth cache.
sources.rule_risk: None. It uses only our own tracks, depth and meshes.

sources.title: S2MDF: A Plug-And-Play Layer for Intersection-Free Multi-Object Signed Distance Fields (Sayin Mercadier, Stella, Bizeau, Talabot, Fua)
sources.verified: Opened the abstract and the full HTML. The constraint is min1(u) + min2(u) ≥ 0, the sum of the two smallest SDFs. Unlike 'second-smallest ≥ 0', it survives linear interpolation, so Marching Cubes output is intersection-free. For K=2 the projection is analytical: if d1 + d2 < 0, add −(d1 + d2)/2 to both. 'Shift-All' generalises this to K>2 with no measurable overhead; QP is exact but raised PartSDF training from 3h30 to 5h40. Measured on MedTet lungs, intersection volume: vanilla 2.28e-5, ObjectSDF++-style soft loss 2.07e-5 (marginal), S2MDF QP 1.35e-9, Shift-All 7.4e-12. Mesh Chamfer about unchanged (6.27 vs 6.10–6.47 e-4). They state soft penalty losses 'reduce but do not eliminate' intersections. No code link found in the paper.
sources.method: Hard projection of a vector of per-object SDF values onto the intersection-free set, usable during training or as post-processing before meshing.
sources.code: None found. The K=2 formula is three lines of numpy.
sources.use_for_us: A guaranteed final safety net so the simulator never starts in penetration. Apply it to our two objects' TSDFs resampled at the end-state relative pose. Caveat derived from our ep24 geometry: the bisector split (d_A = d_B) divides the overlap column diagonally in cross-section, while a slot assembled by sliding must split perpendicular to the insertion axis (see the techniques). Use it only after evidence-based or insertion-based partitioning, never as the partition rule itself.

sources.title: ObjectSDF++: Improved Object-Compositional Neural Implicit Surfaces (Wu et al.)
sources.verified: Opened the abstract and the full HTML. Object distinction regulariser: L_reg = E_p[Σ_{d_i ≠ d_Ω} ReLU(−d_i(p) − d_Ω(p))], applied at random points over the whole volume. Replica ablation (8 scenes, object reconstruction): Chamfer-L1 3.78 → 3.74 and F-score 79.51 → 80.10 with the regulariser, a small gain. The paper motivates it as stopping objects from 'overgrowing in invisible regions like an iceberg'. Code at qianyiwu.github.io/objectsdf++ and github.com/QianyiWu/objectsdf_plus (MIT; training code released, per the GitHub page).
sources.method: Multi-object neural SDF with occlusion-aware opacity rendering and a soft non-overlap loss on unobserved space.
sources.use_for_us: Confirms the principle that unobserved regions of one object must not occupy another object's space. The soft-loss form is weak (S2MDF measured it as marginal). We do not need a neural field; the voxel-level hard carve or projection is better suited to our TSDF.
sources.effort: Not worth porting; take only the principle.
sources.rule_risk: Grey if the monocular priors (pretrained Omnidata) were used; we would not.

sources.title: PhyRecon: Physically Plausible Neural Scene Reconstruction (Ni et al.)
sources.verified: Opened the abstract and the full HTML. A differentiable particle rigid-body simulator (DiffTaichi) drops each object on its support. The physics loss L_phy = Σ_{p∈contact} ||p' − p0|| is applied only to surface points that touch the support, which are the 'unsupported' regions. A physical-uncertainty grid accumulates along contact-point trajectories and drives pixel sampling toward thin structures. Stability success rate in an Isaac Gym drop test: ScanNet++ 26.4 (RICO) / 25.3 (ObjectSDF++) → 78.2; ScanNet 29.7 / 26.6 → 70.3. In the ablation, physics loss alone moves SR 25.3 → 69.0 but 'degenerates shapes' (bulges in unobserved regions). Trained on one A100 for 450 epochs. Code: github.com/PhyRecon/PhyRecon, Apache-2.0, training released 2025-01 (per the GitHub page).
sources.method: Joint differentiable rendering and differentiable physics on per-object SDFs. The support contact during a drop simulation tells the shape where support is missing.
sources.use_for_us: The useful idea is the diagnostic, not the network: simulate a drop of our mesh at the observed rest pose; points that move before first contact mark where the base is missing (the ep18 sweeper underside, ep24 board edges). Our cheaper analogue is to extrude the shape to the support plane observed at rest frames inside the footprint (technique T4). Their failure mode warns that physics-only shape edits create bulges where observation is weak, so restrict edits to unknown voxels.
sources.effort: Full method: days of GPU work, not worth it. The drop-test diagnostic exists in our sim stack: about 0.5 day.
sources.rule_risk: The method uses pretrained monocular normal/depth priors (grey). Our port would not.

sources.title: Betsu-Betsu: Multi-View Separable 3D Reconstruction of Two Interacting Objects
sources.verified: Opened the abstract and the full HTML. Two SDFs share a hashgrid. An alpha-blending regulariser, L_alpha = Σ_p (exp(β/λ_t · α1(p) α2(p)) − 1), penalises points that are opaque for both objects. The ablation reports that without it, 'phantom blobs' form underneath the other object's surface, invisible to rendering but raising Chamfer distance and the human-object 3D IoU. Static multi-view, per frame; no temporal or interaction-motion reasoning. No code link found.
sources.method: Multi-view neural SDF reconstruction of two objects in close contact, with an opacity-product exclusion loss.
sources.use_for_us: Independent evidence that the region hidden at contact gets claimed by the wrong object unless exclusion is enforced. Our filled ep24 notch is that failure. No direct port.

sources.title: ShapeGrasp: Simultaneous Visuo-Haptic Shape Completion and Grasping (Rustler et al.)
sources.verified: Opened the abstract and the full HTML. After each grasp, tactile contacts are added as surface points, and the gripper mesh at its executed pose is added as free-space points (must have SDF > 0). Grasp success 84% (three-finger) and 91% (two-finger). Key negative result: free space from the gripper body hurt when the gripper pose ended up inside the object. Barrett hand Jaccard 55.8% → 52.4% (significant); Robotiq 54.7% → 55.3% (not significant). Tactile alone improved the average by 5.5% (significant). The authors say free space helps only if 'the grasp is precise and does not penetrate'.
sources.method: Implicit-surface shape completion that fuses visual points, contact points and the swept or occupied space of the manipulator.
sources.code: rustlluk.github.io/ShapeGrasp (data and code; licence not checked).
sources.use_for_us: Directly predicts the risk of carving our objects with hand volumes. Our references put the robot hand 16–20 mm (p95) inside objects, so MediaPipe hand-object relative error is likely above our 4 mm voxel. Hand carving must use a shrunken core and be A/B tested; contacts are safer as weak votes only in unknown voxels.

sources.title: Efficient Visuo-Haptic Object Shape Completion for Robot Manipulation (Rustler, Matas, Hoffmann; VISHAC)
sources.verified: Opened the abstract and the full HTML. The robot's traversed space is kept as free points within 20 cm of the object centre. The loss adds |SDF| for free points whose SDF is below 1 mm. Grasp success 63.3% → 70.4% after one touch and 82.7% after five. Code: github.com/ctu-vras/vishac, GPL-3.0 (LICENSE read).
sources.method: Free space traversed by the manipulator, transformed into the object frame, used as a hard-ish SDF > 0 constraint.
sources.use_for_us: The same constraint as Co-Section's hull term, applied to the actor's body. For us the actor is the hand, or the other object, whose swept volume in the object frame is free.

sources.title: HOLD: Category-agnostic 3D Reconstruction of Interacting Hands and Objects from Video (Fan et al.)
sources.verified: Opened the abstract and the full HTML. Compositional implicit hand (MANO-articulated) plus object model. The contact loss L_contact = Σ_i min_j ||V_tips^i − V_o^j|| pulls frequently-contacting fingertip vertices onto the object surface; it is used for pose refinement, not as a shape vote. HO3D: object CD 0.4 cm^2, F10 96.5. Without the hand model: CD 0.41, F10 95.9, and the object gets a hole where the hand occluded it. Without contact pose refinement: CD 0.55, F10 94.2, and hand-relative CD 122.1 vs 11.3. About 10 h on an A100 for the first stage. Code github.com/zc-alexfan/hold, MIT (GitHub page).
sources.method: Joint neural reconstruction of hand and object. Explaining occlusion by the hand removes holes, and fingertip contact fixes relative depth.
sources.use_for_us: Two lessons. (1) Modelling the hand as an occluder (we already drop hand samples) prevents holes. (2) Contact is mainly a relative-pose constraint, which our contact_retarget already uses; using contact as a shape vote is less proven. Full HOLD is far too heavy for us.
sources.rule_risk: Uses a pretrained hand regressor and SfM; MANO licence is non-commercial (grey). We would not use it.

sources.title: NeuralFeels with neural fields: Visuotactile perception for in-hand manipulation (Suresh et al.)
sources.verified: Opened the arXiv abstract: online neural-field SDF plus pose graph fusing vision, touch (DIGIT sensors) and proprioception. Final reconstruction F-score 81%, average pose drift 4.7 mm (2.3 mm with known CAD), up to 94% tracking improvement under heavy occlusion vs vision-only. FeelSight dataset of 70 experiments released.
sources.method: Contact as a direct surface observation in an online SDF.
sources.use_for_us: Shows contact helps when contact geometry is measured (tactile, mm-accurate). Our 'contacts' are MediaPipe keypoints with cm-level error, so treat them as weak priors only.

sources.title: ContactOpt: Optimizing Contact to Improve Grasps (Grady et al.)
sources.verified: Opened the arXiv abstract: a network predicts desired contact on hand and object meshes, then a differentiable contact model optimises hand pose. The model deliberately allows interpenetration to mimic soft tissue. Better contact match, lower kinematic error, preferred by humans. No numbers in the abstract. Repo facebookresearch/contactopt archived 2025-08 (search result, not opened).
sources.method: Contact-driven hand pose optimisation given a known object mesh.
sources.use_for_us: Relevant to contact_retarget (hand placement), not to mesh shape. Its soft-tissue penetration allowance is a reminder that hand-object 'contact' is not a sharp surface (several mm).
sources.rule_risk: Learned contact prior trained on ContactPose (grey; not needed).

sources.title: Directional TSDF: Modeling Surface Orientation for Coherent Meshes (Splietker & Behnke)
sources.verified: Opened the abstract and the full text (ar5iv). It diagnoses that with a standard TSDF, observations from opposite sides of a thin wall contradict within the truncation band, so the object 'blows up' and wrong surfaces appear. The fix stores 6 directional TSDFs (±x, ±y, ±z by normal sector; a sample goes to directions whose weight exceeds sin(π/8), at most 3), uses fusion along surface normals, and a directional marching cubes with voting. RMSE in mm vs state of the art (Stanford models): Asian Dragon at 5 mm voxels 2.34 → 1.56, at 10 mm 7.11 → 2.87; Bunny at 5 mm 1.90 → 0.98. Code: github.com/AIS-Bonn/DirectionalTSDF (InfiniTAM-based, CUDA; LICENSE is the InfiniTAM non-commercial licence).
sources.method: Orientation-binned TSDF so opposite surfaces of thin structures or narrow gaps do not cancel.
sources.use_for_us: Explains two measured defects. (1) Our boards are 3.04 / 3.13 cm thick (oriented bounding box) vs 2.59 / 2.61 cm in the public scans (diagnostic only): about one 4 mm voxel too thick per side, the 'blow-up'. (2) A 1.7 cm notch is narrower than 2 x trunc (24 mm), so every gap voxel sits within 12 mm of a wall and gets negative votes from oblique views. Cheap port in numpy: bin by view direction relative to the object (6 bins), or keep the plain TSDF but give observed free space priority (T3).
sources.effort: 0.5 day for free-space priority; 2–3 days for a numpy directional TSDF.

sources.title: Shape-From-Silhouette Across Time Part I: Theory and Algorithms (Cheung, Baker, Kanade)
sources.verified: Opened the Springer page via curl (meta abstract). It combines all silhouettes of a moving rigid object over time (temporal SFS) once its motion is estimated (visual hull alignment), then refines the visual hull. It extends to articulated objects. The abstract has no numbers. The CMU RI page could not be opened because of a TLS chain error.
sources.method: Visual hull of a moving object: voxels that project outside the object silhouette in any frame (after motion compensation) are free.
sources.use_for_us: We already have 6-DoF tracks, so silhouette carving in the object frame is straightforward once per-frame masks exist. Today masks exist only at frame 0 (perc2.py runs SAM2 at frame 0, FoundationPose tracks after). It recovers profile concavities and sharp edges that the TSDF rounds (board edges, slots seen edge-on, the sweeper base outline). It does not recover concavities never seen in silhouette.
sources.effort: 1–2 days plus GPU (SAM2 video propagation per object per episode).

sources.title: Atlas3D: Physically Constrained Self-Supporting Text-to-3D for Simulation and Fabrication (Chen et al.)
sources.verified: Opened the abstract and the full HTML. Losses: L_stand, a differentiable Warp rigid-body simulation of standing; L_stable, a potential-well test where the centre-of-mass height must not drop when the object is tilted by φ about 20 horizontal axes; normal consistency; and a Laplacian applied only to vertices below height h_b, which flattens the base. Mean TRD (time-averaged rotation deviation) over 107 prompts is reduced more than 6x vs Magic3D. The ablation shows that without L_stand the model falls, and that L_stable raises success under perturbation.
sources.method: Physics-in-the-loop shape refinement for standability plus base-flattening regularisation, on top of SDS (generative).
sources.use_for_us: Two cheap, non-generative pieces port directly. (a) The stable-equilibrium test (CoM height under small tilts) as an automatic accept/reject check for our rest poses. (b) Flattening limited to vertices near the support. The difference for us is that the support plane comes from observation at rest frames, not a prior. This replaces hand-made flatten_base with an episode-driven rule (T4).
sources.rule_risk: The SDS part is a generative prior (grey) and would not be used. The losses and tests are fine.

sources.title: Make It Stand: Balancing Shapes for 3D Fabrication (Prévost, Whiting, Lefebvre, Sorkine-Hornung)
sources.verified: Opened the HAL record (citation_abstract metadata). Balance is formulated as energy minimisation that modifies volume (interior carving plus deformation) while preserving surface detail, so the centre of mass projects into the support. No numbers in the abstract.
sources.method: Static-equilibrium criterion: the CoM projection must lie inside the support polygon; shape and mass edits enforce it.
sources.use_for_us: Gives the acceptance criterion for T4. An object observed resting in a pose must, with our mesh, have its CoM over the support polygon at that pose. If not, the mesh base, the pose, or the density assumption is wrong. Measured earlier on ep24 board 1: CoM 89 mm outside before flattening and marginal after.

sources.title: PhysPart: Physically Plausible Part Completion for Interactable Objects (Luo, Geng et al.)
sources.verified: Opened the abstract and the full HTML. Diffusion part generation guided by a collision loss ℓ_coll = Σ_p ReLU(−X(p) − α) on the object's points, a contact loss, and 'mobility' versions of both averaged over sampled motion states of the part (collision-free along the whole motion, a swept-volume constraint). Physical-plausibility (motion success) without vs with loss guidance: slider drawer 49.3 → 74.3%, hinge door 71.1 → 92.2%, line handle 71.1 → 85.9%, knob 78.9 → 84.2%.
sources.method: Generative part completion with static non-penetration and contact losses plus motion-swept non-penetration.
sources.use_for_us: Supports the swept-volume principle for assemblies. A part that moved along a path must be collision-free with the other part at every state of that path, not just at the end. This is the basis of the insertion-consistent partition (T2) for ep24 slots. The diffusion generator itself is not needed.
sources.rule_risk: The diffusion prior is a pretrained generative model (grey). The loss principle is fine.

sources.title: Ditto: Building Digital Twins of Articulated Objects from Interaction (Jiang, Hsu, Zhu)
sources.verified: Opened the abstract and the ar5iv full text. Given point clouds before and after an interaction, a learned network (PointNet++ plus ConvONet, trained on Shape2Motion-type data) predicts part occupancy, segmentation and joint parameters. Category-agnostic; real objects deployed in simulation. Code github.com/UT-Austin-RPL/Ditto.
sources.method: Learned joint geometry and articulation inference from interaction pairs.
sources.use_for_us: Low. Our objects are rigid; only the 'interaction reveals geometry' framing carries over.
sources.rule_risk: Learned prior trained on synthetic articulated datasets (grey).

sources.title: Neural Shape Mating: Self-Supervised Object Assembly with Adversarial Shape Priors (Chen et al.)
sources.verified: Opened the arXiv abstract: given point clouds of two parts, predict the pair of poses that mate them snugly. Trained on 200K pairs from random mesh cuts. No numbers in the abstract.
sources.use_for_us: The inverse of our problem: we observe the mating poses and need the shapes. Useful only as a later consistency check (do our reconstructed parts mate at the observed pose).

sources.title: Interactive Perception: Leveraging Action in Perception and Perception in Action (Bohg et al.)
sources.verified: Opened the arXiv abstract: a survey defining interactive perception. Interaction creates sensory signals that would otherwise be absent, and regularities between action and sensing help interpret them.
sources.use_for_us: Framing for the write-up: the owner's idea is interactive perception applied to the reconstruction of observed human manipulation.

techniques: T1, cross-object time-max penetration carving (Co-Section d_inter plus VISHAC free space). Implementation: save each object's TSDF and weight grid from recon_mesh. For each other tracked object B, define B's confident core: tsdf <= -0.5 (at least 6 mm deep at trunc 12 mm), weight >= w_min, and not created by closure fill. For every frame t, map A's voxels into B's frame with inv(cam_T_B[t]) @ cam_T_A[t]. Interpolate SE(3) when the relative motion between frames exceeds half a voxel; we measured up to 24 mm/frame on ep24. Compute pen_A(x) = max_t depth_in_core_B(x_t) and set A's voxels with pen_A > margin to free. The margin is the 95th-percentile relative-pose jitter in static assembled segments, measured on ep24 t=220–275 at 0.2–2.3 mm/frame, so about 4 mm. Never carve A's own confident core; flag those conflicts instead. Alternate A and B twice. It targets cavities and slots filled by closure: cup in cup (ep11), cup or pot in the rack (ep12, ep13, ep26, ep27), lid on pot (ep0, ep2), ep24 boards. Falsification: (a) end-state overlap of our meshes in every two-object public episode must drop below 1 cm^3 (ep24 baseline measured 16.2 cm^3 at 2 mm voxels; script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-v2d-track3/8c892c5e-fd7c-57aa-abef-68d2af098e4f/scratchpad/interact/tools/ep24_rel.py). (b) recon_eval mesh vs scan (diagnostic) F-score at 5 mm and Chamfer must not worsen by more than 1 mm for any object. (c) Registered ADD-AUC with our meshes must not drop. If (a) holds but (b) fails, track error exceeds the margin and core carving is eating real material: hypothesis rejected at this tracking accuracy.

T2, insertion-consistent partition of an overlap. New hypothesis derived from Co-Section's time indexing and PhysPart's motion-swept collision loss. Measured on our ep24 tracks: board 2's origin moved 12.9 cm along -y of board 1 (from +12.8 cm at t=160 to 0 at t=220), then stayed fixed. Overlap voxels were penetrated in order along that axis (correlation -0.76 between first-penetration frame and y). The column spans y from -6.0 to +5.4 cm. Rule: if B entered A by translating along -u, any physically valid split of each overlap column along u has the form 'B owns [s, top], A owns [bottom, s)', because every B voxel swept through everything above its final position. Choose s per column from evidence: observed free voxels or TSDF weights of each object in the column. If one object's column is only closure-filled (peg in hole), set s to the bottom. If evidence is equal, use s = midpoint (cross-halving prior). This replaces S2MDF's bisector, which would cut the column diagonally. Falsification: on ep24 this predicts board 1's slot opens toward +y (where board 2 came from) and board 2's slot opens toward -y, each about half the board height (about 6.6 cm of 13.2 cm). Check against the public scans posed by mocap (diagnostic only). Opposite slot sides, or a depth off by more than 2 cm, falsifies the rule. Sim check: the assembled X built from the new meshes starts with zero penetration and stays interlocked when one board is lifted.

T3, observed free space before closure (Co-Section hull constraint; Directional TSDF diagnosis). Keep per-voxel counts n_free (samples with sdf > max(trunc, 2 voxels), meaning the ray clearly passed in front) and n_occ. Mark a voxel free if n_free >= 3 and n_free / (n_free + n_occ) >= 0.3, whatever the averaged TSDF says. --close fill/auto may never fill a voxel with free evidence. Variants: a 6-bin directional TSDF by view direction in the object frame, or trunc 6 mm for objects thinner than 3 cm. Measured motivation (diagnostic): board oriented-bounding-box thickness is 3.04 / 3.13 cm (ours) vs 2.59 / 2.61 cm (scans), about +1 voxel per side, the thin-structure blow-up. Board 2 is also 15.95 x 23.96 cm vs 13.86 x 22.68 cm (scan), which points to spurious material. Falsification: rebuild the ep24 boards (needs the ep24 depth cache). Thickness must come within 2 mm of the scan, and end-state overlap must fall by at least 50% without T1/T2. Also, in pre-assembly frames, count stereo depth pixels inside the projected slot (scan posed by mocap, diagnostic) that hit background. If FoundationStereo never shows background through the 1.7 cm slot (foreground fattening), T3 cannot recover it; T1/T2 are the only route and this hypothesis is falsified for slots.

T4, support-plane closure from observed rest events (PhyRecon contact loss, Atlas3D base flattening and stable-equilibrium test, Make It Stand CoM-in-support-polygon). Detect rest segments: object world speed under 1 mm/frame for at least 15 frames, no hand bone within 3 cm, origin near the table plane. For each, take the table plane π_s in the object frame. Keep the existing below-plane carving, and add three steps. (a) Within the footprint, the convex hull of the projections of the object's observed voxels within 3 cm of π_s, set voxels between π_s and the observed surface to inside (extrude to the plane). (b) In rest frames, let depth samples in the 15 mm table band that fall inside the footprint vote 'surface at the plane' instead of being discarded. Today table_band drops every object sample within 15 mm of the table, which can chop object bottoms; this is a hypothesis for the measured 1–4 cm floating. (c) Accept only if the CoM projection lies inside the resulting support polygon, and CoM height does not drop under ±3° tilts about 20 axes (Atlas3D L_stable as a test). This replaces the hand-made flatten_base, library_v3 and library_v4. Falsification: (1) the ep18 sweeper and both ep24 boards hold their observed rest poses in Newton (tilt under 2°, drift under 5 mm over 2 s) without flatten_base. (2) The lowest-vertex height above the table at rest frames drops from 1–4 cm to under 3 mm. (3) Mesh vs scan does not worsen by more than 1 mm. (4) ep18 registered AUC reaches at least library_v3's 0.715. If (2) still fails after the shape change, the floating is pose error, not shape, and the band hypothesis is rejected.

T5, hand volumes as free space and fingertips as weak contact votes (VISHAC, ShapeGrasp, HOLD). Carve only with a shrunken finger core (about 5 mm radius around MediaPipe bones, not the 30 mm used for sample rejection), only in frames where the hand-object relative pose is steady, and never inside the object's confident core. At grasp frames (object moving with the hand), add fingertip positions as low-weight surface votes, and only into unknown voxels. Prior evidence predicts harm: ShapeGrasp's gripper free space lowered Jaccard from 55.8% to 52.4% when grasps penetrated, and our references show the hand 16–20 mm (p95) inside objects, so expect our hand error to exceed the margin. Falsification and gate: an A/B on ep12, ep18 and ep24 mesh vs scan. If F-score at 5 mm drops, or object volume shrinks by more than 5%, keep it disabled. Run only after T1–T4.

T6, silhouette carving along our tracks (Shape-From-Silhouette across time). Propagate SAM2 masks per object through each episode (GPU). A voxel that projects outside the object's mask in at least k=3 frames, where it is not behind a nearer observed surface, is free. It sharpens rounded board and sweeper edges and opens slots seen in profile, but cannot open concavities never on a silhouette. Falsification: edge radius on ep24 boards (scan-registered, diagnostic) must drop from the current rounded profile toward the scan's, with mesh-vs-scan F-score at 5 mm not decreasing. If mask leakage or hand occlusion carves real material (scan points outside our mesh by more than 3 mm grow by over 5%), reject or raise k.

T7, hard non-penetration safety net (S2MDF, K=2). After T1/T2, resample B's TSDF into A's frame at each end-state and contact frame. Where d_A + d_B < 0, subtract (d_A + d_B)/2 from both, then mesh. Overlap becomes exactly 0 by construction, so the simulator never starts in penetration. Diagnostic and falsification of the earlier steps: log the volume changed by this net. If it exceeds 2 cm^3 on any episode, T1/T2 failed there, and the bisector's diagonal cut will appear as a scan error in the contact region; treat that as a failure, not a fix.

Common protocol for all of the above (inference-legal inputs only; scans and mocap only in the scoring/diagnostic step). For each of the 12 two-object public episodes plus ep39–45, report: (i) end-state overlap volume and time-max penetration depth; (ii) per-object mesh vs scan Chamfer and F-score at 5 mm (diagnostic); (iii) rest-pose stability in Newton; (iv) registered ADD-AUC with our meshes. Report cost (CPU minutes per object) alongside. Prototype locally first on episodes with depth caches (ep2 pot and lid, ep18, ep27 rack and pot, ep39–44). ep24 needs its depth cache fetched before T1–T3 can be measured on the slots.
